First, we note that $w=0$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

We multiply both sides of the equation by $3w,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{2w-3}{3w} & =\frac{w+5}{3w} \\ 3w\cdot (1-\frac{2w-3}{3w}) & =3w\cdot (\frac{w+5}{3w}) \\ 3w\cdot 1-3w\cdot \frac{2w-3}{3w} & =3w\cdot \frac{w+5}{3w} \\ 3w-\cancel{3w}\cdot \frac{2w-3}{\cancel{3w}} & =\cancel{3w}\cdot \frac{w+5}{\cancel{3w}} \\ 3w-(2w-3) & =w+5 \\ 3w-2w+3 & =w+5\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $w,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}3w-2w+3 & =w+5 \\ w+3 & =w+5 \\ w-w & =5-3 \\ 0 & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a false statement. Therefore, we conclude that there is no solution.
